newsitem.title: MEXICO: U.S. investors upbeat toward Mexico - report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. investors upbeat toward Mexico - report.

text.p: Investor confidence toward Mexico has improved markedly over the past year as its economy recovers from the peso crash and investors seek alternatives to record high valuation in U.S. equity markets, according to a survey published on Wednesday.

More than 90 percent of the U.S. market participants said their opinion of Mexican equities had improved substantially from a year ago, according to the survey by Broadgate Consultants Inc. of 30 institutional investors with more than $500 billion under management.
Mexico's early repayment this year to the United States of the controversial bridge loan extended during the peso crisis boosted confidence, the survey said.

Some 86 percent of respondents said they would increase or maintain their weighting of international investment in Mexico this year. Most said the Mexican stock market, trading at a trailing price-earnings multiple of roughly 14.5, was undervalued.
Fears about Mexico's recession have receded and U.S. investors overwhelmingly expect GDP growth of between 4 to 5 percent this year.

"With this kind of GDP growth, U.S. investors believe there are a number of potential industry sector beneficiaries, including construction, telecommunications and financial institutions....(However) questions about the breadth of the recovery remain, particularly with consumer spending perceived to be relatively flat," the survey said.

Despite recent drug corruption scandals, U.S. investors are generally optimistic that progress will be made in rooting out corruption. Although some investors may get nervous ahead of mid-term elections in July, expectations are that they will reflect Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo's commitment to free and fair elections.

Respondents expressed disappointment about the quality of disclosure provided by Mexican companies. They also said Mexican companies can greatly improve their positioning on Wall Street by offering ADRs.
"U.S. investors recognize that Mexico's close proximity makes it one of the most attractive emerging markets," said Thomas Franco, President of Broadgate Consultants.

"But Mexican corporate issuers still have their work cut out for them if they want to build a long-term U.S. investor following that extends beyond the relatively small group of emerging market specialists," he added.
